I will keep my land in the crop pattern I know best: winter wheat followed by summer maize. In Quzhou this fits the weather, the soil, and the way we farm. Winter wheat gives me a steady grain crop, and then summer maize uses the summer heat and rain well. I do not want to spread myself across too many crops, because I am 54, I want simple field work, easy machinery use, and stable income instead of chasing a higher-risk crop. I will use improved seed, not old saved seed, because I want more even emergence and a safer yield, but I will still manage the field in the straightforward way I understand. For wheat, I will plough before sowing, put most phosphorus and potassium in as base fertilizer, split nitrogen between base and topdressing, irrigate at the key stages, and keep disease and aphid control to a few necessary sprays. After wheat harvest, I will rotary-till lightly and plant summer maize quickly to catch moisture. For maize, I will put fertilizer mainly at sowing and jointing, rely mostly on summer rainfall, add irrigation only if the field turns dry, and do only a couple of pesticide applications if weeds, borers, or leaf disease become a real problem. I am choosing a stable, familiar grain rotation and moderate input level, because that is the plan I would trust myself to carry through well.
